Honoré de Balzac, Letters of Two Brides, translated by R. S. Scott.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/honore-de-balzac/letters-of-two-brides/r-s-scott

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Honoré de Balzac, the author, died 1850 or 1851 (Wikidata Q9711, P570 1850-08-18 and 1851-08-19).
- R. S. Scott, the translator, died 1905 (Wikidata Q19325151, P570 1905-11-27).

First publication of the text used: 1901, the English translation by R. S. Scott. The French original was published in 1841. The country of first publication of the translation is not stated in the facts. (SE colophon: 'Letters of Two Brides was published in 1841 by Honoré de Balzac. It was translated from French in 1901 by R. S. Scott.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the translation was first published in 1901 and the original in 1841, both before 1931, so the text is in the United States public domain. The edition's rights statement quoted below says the same.
- Country of origin: Every person whose words are in the text died in 1925 or earlier (Honoré de Balzac, the author, died 1850 or 1851; R. S. Scott, the translator, died 1905), so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less. The country of first publication does not matter. The translator is identified by the Standard Ebooks link to Wikidata Q19325151 in the facts. The original is public domain in every country because its author died before 1926.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon of this edition (https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/honore-de-balzac/letters-of-two-brides/r-s-scott): quoted above.
- Wikidata Q9711 (Honoré de Balzac), P570 1850-08-18 and 1851-08-19.
- Wikidata Q19325151 (R. S. Scott), P570 1905-11-27.
